cards.heading: Definition — dual expression
cards.question: What is build-time generation governance's core mechanism for constraining what a coding agent produces?
cards.answer: Every structural invariant and threat vector is declared once and expressed twice: as prose compiled into the agent's context (biases generation softly) and as a deterministic static rule, e.g. Semgrep/CodeQL/Bandit, in the pipeline (rejects violations mechanically at merge, regardless of what the model produced).

cards.heading: Why scope artifacts per module
cards.question: Why does a compiler step scope which governance artifacts apply to which module, instead of concatenating every document into one prompt?
cards.answer: A context window crowded with competing constraints degrades what the model attends to — scoping keeps only the relevant boundaries in view for a given module.

cards.heading: Conflict resolution
cards.question: When declared governance artifacts conflict, how is the conflict resolved?
cards.answer: Deterministically, before assembly, not by the model reconciling documents: threat model outranks structural boundaries, boundaries outrank coding standards, standards outrank feature intent. The conflict then surfaces as a failed build, and a human changes the design.

cards.heading: Two gates
cards.question: What are the two gates that run against agent-generated code, and why are both needed?
cards.answer: An adversarial check (no declared abuse path was opened) and an acceptance check against machine-executable scenarios (the declared business contract was met). Without the adversarial gate the system can violate its structure; without the acceptance gate it can faithfully implement the wrong thing.

cards.heading: Limits of static rules
cards.question: What can build-time static rules never verify, and what practical consequence follows from that limit?
cards.answer: They can't verify domain semantics, aggregate ownership, or conceptual cohesion — only compliance with what was declared. Consequence: a stale or wrong governance artifact is enforced just as faithfully as a correct one, so these artifacts must be treated as production code with owners, versioning and peer review.
